subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should shared-token/password WebSocket operator clients without device identity ever receive operator scopes on non-local connections, and if so through which bounded policy?
rationale: Current tests and docs intentionally clear self-declared scopes for this class of device-less connection, while the user report shows real remote operator workflows need a trusted path; choosing that trust boundary is a maintainer security/product decision.

options.title: Land bounded token scopes
options.body: Add or land a documented gateway.auth.tokenScopes-style policy with exposure guards, tests, and proof for trusted headless/shared-token deployments.

options.title: Preserve shared-token scopes
options.body: Treat successful token/password WebSocket auth as sufficient to retain declared operator scopes, accepting the broader shared-secret trust boundary.

options.title: Require device identity
options.body: Keep clearing device-less self-declared scopes and document that remote clients must use approved device identity/device tokens for write access.

recommendation.title: Land bounded token scopes
recommendation.body: Add or land a documented gateway.auth.tokenScopes-style policy with exposure guards, tests, and proof for trusted headless/shared-token deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the active tokenScopes implementation path and recent Gateway shared-auth decisions in this area.
